messages.subject: covariate detection probabilities
parts:
Hello List,

I am a new DISTANCE user so please forgive my ignorance.

I am using multiple covariate distance sampling model to obtain
probabilities of detection at different Beaufort Sea States (0-4) along a
trackline. I have managed to import the data correctly and run analyses
without errors. However, I cannot get the detection probabilities for each
sea state at different distances out of the results. The plots visually
describe the data I want, but I can't seem to get the values. Is my only
chance to plug distance values into each function of each sea state? If so,
I would appreciate any guidance on that step.

Thank you all so much for any advice. Please send email responses to
lg...@duke.edu.

Cheers,
Leigh


Leigh Torres
PhD Candidate

messages.author: 5900eadecec2d82d
messages.subject: Re: covariate detection probabilities
parts:
Hi Leigh, list,

It is quite easy to get estimated detection probability at a given distance:

(A)You can get the actual values used in the plots in one of two ways:
- (1) When a plot is showing in the analysis details window, right click and
choose "Copy plot to clipboard", or click on the "Copy current window to
clipboard" button on the main toolbar. Then open a text file or a spreadsheet
and do a paste.
- (2) In the model definition properties, under Detection Function |
Diagnostics, tick the button to "Create file of histogram data".
To find out what the various columns mean, look in the online help index under
"Plot file".

(B) You can also work out the value by hand, using the parameter estimates, as
you indicate. For more about this, and a worked example, look in the online
help index under "Detection Function" | "About formulae".

Another thing you might want is an estimate of average probability of
detection within the surveyed area (ie between 0 and w, the truncation
distance). This is a bit harder and unfortunately Distance doesn't give it
for each level of a factor covariate. One approach would be to take the
average of the values output from the plotting functions, above. A more
accurate approach would be to use a stats or maths package to integrate the
detection function using the parameter estimate values given by Distance.
There is a bit about this in the online topic "Calculating effective strip
width", which is the page after the one that tells you about calculating
detection function formulae (reall that average probability of detection is
effective strip width over trucation distance, for line transects).

Hope this helps,

- Len
